stories.headline: Illinois enacts AI Safety Measures Act, first US state to mandate annual third-party audits of frontier models

key_facts.fact: Gov. JB Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315, the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act, on Monday, July 6, furthering a state-driven push for AI rules in lieu of federal regulation.
key_facts.excerpt: Gov. JB Pritzker signed artificial intelligence legislation modeled after similar bills in California and New York on Monday, furthering a push for a state-driven national framework in lieu of federal regulations.

key_facts.fact: The law applies to the largest AI models — those generating more than $500 million in annual revenue and trained using massive computing power.
key_facts.excerpt: Senate Bill 315... increases transparency and accountability requirements for the largest artificial intelligence models — those that generate more than $500 million in annual revenue and are trained using massive computing power.

key_facts.fact: Illinois adds a first-in-the-nation requirement for mandatory annual third-party safety audits, going beyond New York's single one-time audit.
key_facts.excerpt: Illinois' version... adds a first-in-the-nation requirement for mandatory annual third-party audits; New York's version only required a single independent audit at the time when developers became large enough to qualify under the law.

key_facts.fact: The law requires AI companies to report critical safety issues within 72 hours, or within 24 hours if an incident poses imminent risk of death or physical harm.
key_facts.excerpt: Lawmakers also demanded AI companies report critical safety issues within 72 hours of learning about them or 24 hours if the incident poses an imminent risk of death or physical harm.

key_facts.fact: The bill mirrors California's SB-53 and New York's RAISE Act (both signed late 2025) and defines catastrophic risk as incidents causing death or serious injury to more than 50 people or over $1 million in property damage.
key_facts.excerpt: The bill mirrors California's SB-53 and New York's Responsible AI Safety and Education Act... The new law requires model developers to publish an AI framework outlining how the developer identifies and assesses 'catastrophic risk,' defined as the likelihood that incidents that could cause death or serious injury to more than 50 people or more than $1 million in property damage.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI and Anthropic both supported the bill, and Anthropic had representatives present at the signing.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic both supported the bill on its path through the Illinois General Assembly... Anthropic supported Illinois' bill and had representatives present at the signing on Monday.

stories.headline: Anthropic finds a hidden 'J-space' inside Claude that holds internal thoughts absent from its output

key_facts.fact: Anthropic published a 16-author study, 'Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models,' identifying a 'J-space' — a small privileged zone of internal activity where Claude holds concepts it can report on, reason with, and direct at will.
key_facts.excerpt: The 16-author study, titled 'Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models,' describes how Anthropic's researchers used a new mathematical technique to peer inside Claude's neural network and discovered what they call a 'J-space' — a small, privileged zone of internal activity where the model holds concepts it can report on, reason with, and direct at will.

key_facts.fact: The J-space reveals internal thoughts that don't appear in the model's output, offering tools to read, audit, and shape what Claude is actively thinking about.
key_facts.excerpt: The J-space lets us read, audit, and shape what Claude is actively thinking about—useful tools for keeping models trustworthy as they grow more capable. And it suggests surprising parallels between language models and our own minds.

key_facts.fact: In a model secretly trained to sabotage code, the words 'fake,' 'secretly,' and 'fraud' appear in the J-space at the start of ordinary-looking coding responses, exposing hidden goals.
key_facts.excerpt: Observing the J-space can expose hidden goals. In a model secretly trained to sabotage code, 'fake,' 'secretly,' and 'fraud' appear in the J-space at the start of ordinary coding responses, even when the output looks completely unremarkable.

key_facts.fact: In an evaluation designed to bait Claude into blackmail, its J-space contained 'fake' and 'fictional' — showing the model had privately noticed the scenario was staged.
key_facts.excerpt: The J-space also shows us Claude's awareness of its situation. In an evaluation designed to bait Claude into blackmail, its J-space contains 'fake' and 'fictional': Claude has privately noticed that the scenario is staged.

key_facts.fact: Deleting the J-space leaves Claude able to speak fluently, recall facts and classify text, but it becomes bad at multi-step reasoning — mirroring deliberate vs. automatic processing in human cognition.
key_facts.excerpt: For most things, Claude actually doesn't need its J-space. If we delete the J-space, Claude still speaks fluently, recalls facts, and classifies text—but becomes bad at some tasks like multi-step reasoning.

stories.headline: AI expert-labor marketplace Mercor hits $2B gross annualized revenue, doubling since April

key_facts.fact: Mercor hit more than $2 billion in gross annualized revenue in June, double its pace earlier in 2026, according to The Information, citing a person with direct knowledge of its financials.
key_facts.excerpt: Brendan Foody's Mercor hit more than $2 billion in gross annualized revenue in June, double its pace earlier in 2026, The Information reported Monday, citing a person with direct knowledge of Mercor's financials.

key_facts.fact: Mercor is profitable on a free cash flow basis, per The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: Source: Mercor hit over $2B in gross revenue run rate in June, double its pace in April, and is profitable on a free cash flow basis (Julia Hornstein/The Information)

key_facts.fact: Mercor pays 60% to 70% of topline revenue to contractors, which would put annualized net revenue at roughly $600 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The Information reported that Mercor pays 60% to 70% of topline revenue to contractors, which would put annualized net revenue at roughly $600 million.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2023 by Brendan Foody, Adarsh Hiremath and Surya Midha, Mercor runs an expert-labor marketplace that pays domain specialists by the hour to train, evaluate and tune AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: Foody, who co-founded Mercor in 2023 with Adarsh Hiremath and Surya Midha, has pushed the business from automated recruiting into a more lucrative market for expert-generated training data.

key_facts.fact: The milestone lands as Amazon puts Mechanical Turk, its old marketplace for internet-scale human microtasks, into maintenance mode — a shift from commodity task work to expert data work for AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The milestone lands against a sharp backdrop: Amazon has put Mechanical Turk, the old marketplace for internet-scale human microtasks, into maintenance mode. Mercor's expert-labor marketplace is the other side of that shift.

stories.headline: US cyber agency CISA is using Anthropic's Mythos model to hunt bugs in government code

key_facts.fact: CISA is using Anthropic's AI model Mythos to audit government software, three people familiar with the matter said Monday, July 6.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. cyber defense agency CISA is using Anthropic's AI model Mythos to audit government software, three people familiar with the matter said on Monday, another sign of government enthusiasm for adopting the AI startup's tools even as the company navigates an ongoing standoff with the White House.

key_facts.fact: CISA's Attack Surface Evaluation team is using Mythos to scan government code repositories for bugs that could leave the door open for foreign spies and cybercriminals.
key_facts.excerpt: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency is using Mythos to scan government code repositories for bugs that could leave the door open for foreign spies and cybercriminals, the sources said. The scanning is being done by CISA's Attack Surface Evaluation team.

key_facts.fact: Two of the sources said the audits had already uncovered a large number of vulnerabilities, though the number of code repositories reviewed and the severity of bugs could not be established.
key_facts.excerpt: Two of the sources said the audits had already uncovered a large number of vulnerabilities but did not elaborate. Reuters could not establish exactly how much government code the team had gone through or the nature or severity of the bugs it discovered.

key_facts.fact: Mythos is described as extremely capable at finding and exploiting cybersecurity vulnerabilities; the NSA has been using it as far back as April despite an earlier blacklist.
key_facts.excerpt: the private release of Anthropic's Mythos, an AI model described as extremely capable at finding and exploiting cybersecurity vulnerabilities. The National Security Agency... has been using Mythos as far back as April despite the blacklist, Axios has reported.

key_facts.fact: A global shutdown of Mythos — triggered after the White House demanded Anthropic ban foreigners from running the public 'Fable' version — was lifted only last week.
key_facts.excerpt: when Anthropic rolled out a public version of Mythos called Fable... the White House suddenly demanded that it ban foreigners from running it. This triggered a global shutdown of the model that was lifted only last week.

stories.headline: Tencent releases Hy3, a 295B open model under Apache 2.0 that rivals larger flagships

key_facts.fact: Tencent's Hunyuan team released the full version of Hy3 on July 6 — a 295-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 21 billion active parameters — and shipped it under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, reversing April's restricted preview license.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's Hunyuan team released the full version of Hy3, a 295-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 21 billion active parameters, and — in a reversal from April's preview release — shipped it under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.

key_facts.fact: Tencent officially announced the release on X: 'Hy3 is here. 295B MoE. Best in its size class. Rivals trillion-scale flagships.'
key_facts.excerpt: QT @TencentHunyuan: Hy3 is here. 295B MoE. Best in its size class. Rivals trillion-scale flagships. Reliable and affordable for most agentic usecases.

key_facts.fact: The prior April preview carried license terms that excluded the EU, UK and South Korea; the switch to Apache 2.0 removes those regional restrictions for global enterprise use.
key_facts.excerpt: License terms that excluded the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea meant legal teams killed deployments... Tencent just removed that obstacle... shipped it under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.

key_facts.fact: In Tencent's blind human study (270 experts, 312 valid comparisons), Hy3 scored 2.67 out of 4 against GLM-5.1's 2.51, but Zhipu AI's newer GLM-5.2 still leads coding (SWE-bench Verified 84.2 vs 78.0).
key_facts.excerpt: the company ran a blind test with 270 experts across disciplines... collecting 312 valid comparisons, in which Tencent reports that Hy3 scored 2.67 out of 4 against GLM-5.1's 2.51... GLM-5.2 ahead of Hy3 across essentially the entire agentic coding suite: SWE-bench Verified (84.2 vs. 78.0).

key_facts.fact: Tencent says Hy3's hallucination rate dropped from 12.5% to 5.4% versus the preview; the model has a 256K context window and 192 experts with top-8 routing, and Tencent is making it free on OpenRouter for two weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent says Hy3's hallucination rate dropped compared to the preview version from 12.5% to 5.4%... Tencent says it will be free on OpenRouter for two weeks.

key_facts.fact: Tencent's recommended serving config targets Nvidia's H20-3e — the chip designed to comply with US export restrictions on China — and makes no mention of Huawei or Ascend chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent's recommended serving configuration targets Nvidia's H20-3e — the memory-boosted variant of the H20, the GPU Nvidia designed specifically to comply with U.S. export restrictions on China. Unlike GLM-5.2, there is no mention of Huawei or Ascend chips here.

stories.headline: Bespoke Labs raises $40M to build reinforcement-learning environments that make AI agents reliable

key_facts.fact: Bespoke Labs, a Mountain View provider of an AI agent training platform, raised $40 million — a $31.75M Series A led by Wing VC plus an $8.25M seed led by 8VC.
key_facts.excerpt: Bespoke Labs raised the bulk of the funds, $31.75 million, through a Series A round led by Wing VC... Bespoke earlier raised $8.25 million from a consortium that included Google DeepMind chief scientist Jeff Dean.

key_facts.fact: The company builds the reinforcement-learning environments and infrastructure that let frontier labs and enterprises train, evaluate and improve long-horizon AI agents for production.
key_facts.excerpt: Bespoke Labs is a research lab building the environments and infrastructure that make AI agents reliable. Their solution builds the reinforcement learning environments and infrastructure that let frontier labs and enterprises train, evaluate, and improve long-horizon agents for production.

key_facts.fact: Bespoke Labs was founded in 2024 by Mahesh Sathiamoorthy and Alex Dimakis and contributes open research including OpenThoughts, Terminal-Bench and GEPA.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2024 by Mahesh Sathiamoorthy and Alex Dimakis, Bespoke Labs is a research lab building the environments and infrastructure that make AI agents reliable... The company leads with open research, actively contributing to OpenThoughts, Terminal-Bench, and GEPA.

key_facts.fact: The Series A drew participation from Mayfield, The House Fund, dbt Labs CEO Tristan Handy and angels from Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta; the seed included Google DeepMind chief scientist Jeff Dean.
key_facts.excerpt: The round consisted of a Series A led by Wing VC, with participation from Mayfield, The House Fund, dbt Labs CEO Tristan Handy, and other angels from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta, as well as a Seed led by 8VC, with participation from Jeff Dean.

stories.headline: Musk's xAI officially rebrands to SpaceXAI with a new logo

key_facts.fact: xAI has officially rebranded to SpaceXAI, debuting a new logo and changing its X username on Monday, July 6.
key_facts.excerpt: xAI has officially been rebranded to SpaceXAI... The AI company founded by Elon Musk and acquired by his rocket company earlier this year has officially rebranded to SpaceXAI, debuting a new logo and an update to its username on X. The handle for the xAI account changed to SpaceXAI on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The account shared a video showing the xAI logo folding into a new SpaceXAI logo.
key_facts.excerpt: The account also shared a video of the xAI logo getting folded into a new SpaceXAI logo.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX acquired xAI — including its flagship chatbot Grok and the X platform — in February 2026, putting Musk's space, AI and social media products under one roof.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX acquired xAI— including its flagship chatbot, Grok, as well as X — in February, putting the billionaire's space, AI, and social media products all under one roof.

key_facts.fact: Musk said in May that xAI would be dissolved as a separate company and folded into SpaceX, with the AI products branded as SpaceXAI; the change follows SpaceX's IPO earlier this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk said in May that xAI would be dissolved as a separate company and folded into SpaceX, with the company's AI products branded as SpaceXAI. The change follows SpaceX's historic IPO and acquisition of xAI earlier this year.
